transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maeve Carter (Redwood AE), Jonah Patel (Redwood SE), Iris Gomez (Redwood CSM); Liam Torres (Nova Orbit CTO), Priya Shah (ML Eng), Alex Nguyen (DevOps), Rashmi Iyer (Product)

Summary (auto): Quick intro, qualification on current stack (OpenAI evals, internal cost concerns), ask about time-to-first-token and ease of onboarding. Agreement to run short pilot with free credits.

[00:00] Maeve: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maeve from redwood, i'll be your AE today, with jonah our se and iris from CS. excited to learn about nova orbit and see how we can help with inference cost and latency.
[00:22] Liam: thanks, yeah appreciate it. quick context, we're building a realtime summarization feature across flight telem data, latency matter a lot, cost is also a show stopper. we've been poking at openai but want more control and better price predictability.
[00:40] Jonah: cool, priya, alex, curious about your stack today? what are you using for inference, seq lengths, qps?
[00:52] Priya: right now a mix — prototyping with OpenAI gpt-4, but for production we're looking at smaller open models on premise and was evaluating bedrock a bit. typical prompt size ~120 tokens, responses ~80 tokens, peaks 60 req/s during batch windows, but steady 6-8 req/s for UI endpoints.
[01:18] Alex: infra is k8s on aws, we have private vpc and strict egress rules — anything we run needs SAML, kms integration, and audit logs for compliance.
[01:33] Maeve: perfect, that's exactly the kind of profile Redwood sees a lot. our plg quickstart is designed to get you to a first token in minutes — SDKs (python/node) + hosted api + free credits. if you need VPC/private, that's our Private offering, and Dedicated sits in the middle for reserved capacity.
[01:55] Liam: ok so two quick questions: 1) how fast can we test — like time-to-first-token? 2) if we go hosted, concerns about data retention and residency, what are the controls?
[02:10] Iris: great questions — time-to-first-token is usually <10 minutes for engineers who run our quickstart guide: sign up, add api key, run sample request. we can provision a trial org and preload free credits so your team can run benchs. for data, hosted keeps request logs for X days configurable; for stricter controls we offer Private (VPC + customer KMS) and Dedicated with guaranteed isolation.
[02:34] Priya: when you say "X days" what's the default retention? and is there an easy way to disable logs for PII?
[02:42] Jonah: default is 30 days for logs in hosted, but you can disable persistent logging on some endpoints; Private gives you full control. also audit logs and SAML/SCIM SSO are available for enterprise plans.
[02:56] Rashmi: curious about perf — you mentioned batching and kv cache, how do you handle realtime usecases where we can't batch much?
[03:08] Jonah: yeah so the runtime supports continuous batching but for low-latency paths we optimize single-request paths and offer model routing — you can pin lower-latency variants or smaller quantized models. there are tradeoffs: smaller quantized models reduce cost and latency but may shift quality slightly.
[03:31] Liam: perf numbers? any ballpark token latency on gpus you support?
[03:37] Jonah: ballpark on a 8k seq LLM variant — cold first-token latency on our hosted endpoints can be ~80-120ms per token for optimized models; steady-state is lower with KV cache. for ultra-low-latency we can benchmark dedicated pools and show end-to-end p95 numbers — happy to run that as part of the demo.
[03:58] Liam: ok good.
[04:02] Priya: what's the onboarding friction if we prefer to start hosted and move to private later? is config portable?
[04:11] Maeve: portability is a big focus — same api/route config across hosted, dedicated and private. you'll pin model versions and rollout policies in the control plane, so migration is mostly a config switch and re-pointing. we also provide a migration playbook.
[04:28] Alex: network-wise, if we go Private, do you run anything in our vpc or do we need to install an agent?
[04:36] Jonah: Private can be deployed as a customer-managed control plane in your VPC or an on-prem package for air-gapped. we integrate with your KMS/HSM for keys. there is an installer + terraform modules, our solutions team helps with setup.
[04:51] Rashmi: security compliance — do you have SOC2 and ISO? and can we get pen-test reports?
[04:58] Iris: yes SOC2 Type II, we also have ISO in progress, we can share security pack and pen-test summary under NDA.
[05:08] Liam: what's cost model during the trial — i.e. free credits, limits, quotas?
[05:14] Maeve: we give trial orgs free credits tied to a time window and per-route quotas to prevent accidental spend. the quickstart page we send has details. after the trial, hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved monthly.
[05:29] Priya: can you do embeddings as well? we have vector search for telemetry semantics.
[05:34] Jonah: yes — embeddings, chat, structured output and reranking are supported. we also provide batching recommendations and cache profiles in Redwood Optimize to bring down unit cost.
[05:47] Alex: any SDK examples for node? we predominantly build frontend apps that call our backend.
[05:53] Maeve: yes, node + python examples, we'll share a minimal example that does an auth'd fetch and streams tokens. time-to-first-token for a developer following the guide is typically under 10 minutes.
[06:05] Liam: would like to see a live demo of the quickstart flow and then a deeper perf session. could you show the sample flow now?
[06:12] Maeve: sure quick screen share — "maeve is sharing screen" (brief pause) — here's the quickstart docs, sign up screen, create api key, paste example curl. you run it and you get a streamed response.
[06:40] [brief cross-talk, someone drops audio for ~5s then returns]
[06:52] Maeve: apologies, i think jonah's camera glitched. okay so after sign-up you have an org dashboard with credits and routes. we can also pre-provision org and credits for your trial.
[07:05] Priya: can you pre-configure an endpoint with a model pinned for us to hit for benchmarking?
[07:11] Iris: yes we can create a route and give you the api key, or you can self-serve and we'll top up credits.
[07:19] Liam: on benchmarking, we need p50/p95 numbers and cost per 1k tokens at our workload. can you handle per-route analytics?
[07:28] Jonah: yes console gives token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. we'll run a short benchmark with your prompts to get realistic p95.
[07:40] Priya: small tangent — for private deployments, how do you handle model weights? do we have to host weights ourselves?
[07:47] Jonah: depends — with Private you can bring-your-own-model weights or we can provide validated open model variants. for highly regulated settings teams often host weights in their own infra with our runtime.
[07:59] Alex: curious about fallback behavior — if a region is throttled do you have automatic fallbacks?
[08:05] Maeve: yes smart routing can failover to compatible model variants or other regions per policy.
[08:12] Rashmi: what about RBAC and team controls? we need least-privilege for keys.
[08:18] Iris: SSO + SCIM provisioning, granular API keys with route scope, and token-level permissions are supported.
[08:26] Liam: ok looks promising. what's a typical pilot we run?
[08:31] Maeve: most pilots are 2-4 weeks: quickstart + run benchs, then a dedicated demo to go over p95/p50 and quality. if you need dedicated capacity we scope a small reserved pool.
[08:44] Priya: will you help with prompt/quality evals? we have some hallucination sensitivity.
[08:50] Jonah: yes our optimize tooling can help with regressions, and we can tie quality alerts to prompt sets/evals. we'll also share sample eval harnesses.
[08:59] Liam: any gotchas for migrating later from hosted to dedicated/private? downtime?
[09:04] Jonah: typically minimal — it's more of a config switch and re-deploy of model endpoints; we recommend a canary rollout and keep fallbacks. we help with migration runbook.
[09:18] Rashmi: curious about pricing on Dedicated — is it always monthly reserved or any hourly bursts?
[09:25] Maeve: Dedicated is reserved monthly with burst capacity options for spikes. pricing varies by pool size and GPU type. we'll share a baseline pricing sheet.
[09:36] Alex: one more infra q: do you support VPC peering or PrivateLink?
[09:41] Jonah: we support VPC peering and private connections; specifics depend on region, we'll include details in the security pack.
[09:51] Liam: ok what do you need from us to start the trial?
[09:55] Maeve: ideally a small list: names of engineers to invite, sample prompt set and target SLA (p95 latency), and any compliance redlines. we'll provision a trial org and credits.
[10:08] Priya: we'll put together a 50-sample prompt file and target p95 < 400ms.
[10:14] Liam: and can we request to benchmark against our current openai setup to compare latency and cost?
[10:20] Jonah: absolutely — upload your samples and we'll run a side-by-side on comparable model variants.
[10:28] Rashmi: are there any limitations on streaming token length for hosted? we have some long outputs.
[10:33] Jonah: streaming supports long outputs; we expose chunking and backpressure controls. sequence length limits depend on model choice.
[10:41] Maeve: ok quick recap and next steps: 1) Iris will provision trial org + credits 2) Maeve will share pricing + pilot template 3) Jonah will schedule a dedicated performance demo and benchmark 4) Nova Orbit to upload sample prompts and target SLAs.
[10:58] Liam: sounds good. anything else?
[11:01] Priya: one small note — are there any SDK rate limits on free trial?
[11:06] Iris: trial orgs have conservative per-route quotas to protect from runaway, but we'll set it to match your expected qps for the pilot.
[11:16] Alex: please include a checklist for security docs access.
[11:19] Maeve: yep will include. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invite for the benchmark demo.
[11:27] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "kv cash" instead of "kv cache"), brief audio drop at ~06:40, some speaker labels may be simplified.
